outcome: Global regularity for the classical relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell system with large, general (non-symmetric) initial data remains open as of September 2026; all developments found in the window are either about restricted/symmetric cases whose core result predates the window, or about a distinct modified/related system.
summary: The bullet asks about regularity of solutions of the classical relativistic Vlasov-Maxwell (RVM) system, i.e. whether smooth solutions with large, general initial data remain smooth for all time. This is a long-standing open problem (Glassey-Strauss era continuation criteria, still the state of the art in spirit). I searched extensively for any 2024-2026 development and found three categories of activity, none of which changes the status of the general problem: (1) A 2025/2026 paper by Constantin and Grayer (arXiv:2504.01687, published in Communications in Mathematical Physics 2026) proves unconditional global regularity for large data, but for a 'Radiative Vlasov-Maxwell' system in which the Lorentz force is modified by an added radiation-reaction damping term. This is a different (related) system, not the classical RVM system this bullet refers to — per the scope rule (§3.1), a modified system with an added damping mechanism that the authors themselves note is what makes the problem tractable is a variant, not a case, of the stated question. (2) Xuecheng Wang's large-data global existence result for the RVM system restricted to cylindrical symmetry was originally posted to arXiv as 2203.01199 v1 in March 2022 — before the frozen revision date of 26 January 2024 — and already contained the full global existence claim. In July 2026 the author reformatted and split this into a two-part sequence (revised 2203.01199 as 'Part I' and a new companion arXiv:2607.14685 as 'Part II', which independently derives pointwise estimates that were treated as black boxes in the original). This is a restructuring and strengthening of rigor for an already-existing 2022 result, not a new mathematical event within the window; even if it were treated as new, cylindrical symmetry is a restriction (a case) of the general problem, which remains open outside that symmetry class. (3) A search for AI involvement turned up arXiv:2603.15929 ('Semi-Autonomous Formalization of the Vlasov-Maxwell-Landau Equilibrium', Ilin, March 2026), a striking AI-assisted Lean formalization using Gemini DeepThink, Claude Code, and the Aristotle prover — but this addresses equilibrium characterization for the Vlasov-Maxwell-Landau system, a different question about a different (collisional, Landau-damping) system, not the regularity/global-existence question this bullet asks about. No AI system was found to be involved in any work on the classical Vlasov-Maxwell regularity problem itself. I did not find the problem's own dedicated Wikipedia article (the general Vlasov-Maxwell equations article does not discuss the regularity question), so I relied on the arXiv literature and continuation-criterion papers (e.g. Luk-Strain, Cheverry-Ibrahim) directly.
competing_reading: One could argue the July 2026 Part I/Part II restructuring of Wang's cylindrical-symmetry result constitutes a new 'event' worth dating to 2026 as `progress`, since Part II's independently-derived pointwise estimates were not previously public and arguably strengthen the original 2022 argument's rigor. Under that reading the status might be `partial` (a symmetric case newly solidified) dated to July 2026. I did not adopt this reading because the mathematical claim (global existence for large cylindrically-symmetric data) was already asserted and essentially argued in the 2022 v1, so the substantive resolution of that case predates the window; the 2026 papers are presentation/rigor work on a pre-existing result.
what_would_settle_it: A statement from Wang or independent experts on whether the 2022 v1 proof was considered complete/correct before the 2026 Part II estimates were supplied, or whether the pointwise estimates in Part II were a genuinely new, previously-missing ingredient without which the 2022 claim did not hold up. That would decide whether the cylindrical-symmetry case should be dated 2022 (open_stale) or 2026 (partial/progress).
